summary: 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 on an active Arkansas Forestry site in Bradley County; a 1952 survey describes a steel structure about 110 ft high at the Bucksnort station.

access.note: Register calls it an active Arkansas Forestry site; the sources read state no public visiting rule

events.note: 1952 survey description of Bucksnort (AFC 4-1): four-legged steel structure with 6 by 6 foot cabin, about 110 feet high to roof apex; not a build date

evidence.quote: This 100ft Aermotor MC-39 is located at an active Arkansas Forestry site
The lower level stairs have been removed.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1952 (JCM)

evidence.supports: steel structure supporting 6 x 6 foot cabin, about 110 feet high
evidence.quote: STEEL STRUCTURE SUPPORTING A 6 X 6 FOOT CABIN ABOUT 110 FEET
THE POINT INTERSECTED WAS THE APEX OF THE ROOF.

evidence.quote: THE STATION IS ABOUT 3-1/2 MILES SOUTHWEST OF HERMITAGE

evidence.quote: spent the daylight hours scanning the forests for signs of smoke

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register describes a 100ft Aermotor MC-39; the 1952 survey describes the steel structure with cabin about 110 feet high to the roof apex. The story reports both; the brief's 33.5 m is kept and sourced to the 1952 record.

notes_for_editor: The history is thin. The 1952 Bucksnort (AFC 4-1) record is linked to this tower only by the Forestry Commission and Bradley County. The NGS record has no coordinates; it places the station about 3-1/2 miles southwest of Hermitage and 1 mile northwest of State Highway 15. The Register coordinates (N 33.418480, W 092.217680) were not checked against that position on a map. Two WebSearch calls found nothing on a Bradley County tower. The AFC Bradley County county page returned 404. Leads: AFC Bradley County office in Hermitage; 1955 state operations map at the State Archives (search result, not read).
